text:
Ava: Quick sync — planning final benchmark tiles for launch. Goal: show a tight "latency -> $/token" thread with actionable CTAs. Keep it short and data-first.
Noah: Proposed kit: 1) density scatter (latency vs $/k tokens), 2) 95th-tail histogram, 3) example bill calculator. Three short lines of copy per tile.
Priya: Landing tests: 'Estimate your cost' vs 'Get free credits and run' as CTAs. Also consider a microcase for customer types (startup, scale, enterprise).
Leo: I'll run a short run: 30-minute window, 100 concurrent websocket chat sessions, using production-like prompt distributions. Will anonymize traces.
Taylor: On visuals: aiming for horizontal tiles for mobile. Colors: green for fastest, indigo for balanced, amber for cheapest. Need raw CSV.
Noah: Add a tiny explainer: batching + prefix cache assumptions. People react badly to unknowns.
Ava: Tone: one bold claim + one supporting stat. Example claim: 'Instant-feel chat at scale'. Supporting stat should be exact: median 90ms / 95th 320ms on our microbench.
Priya: For messaging tests, try one CTA variant that emphasizes dollars, another that emphasizes latency. We can wire both to different UTM params.
Leo: Run command I'm using for reproducibility:
```bash
./bin/bench_chat --concurrency 100 --duration 1800 --model redwood-large --quant q5_0 --cache-prefix true --out bench_6823.csv
```
Leo: Will also attach a tiny assumptions.txt: model param count, tokenization rules, average prompt length.
Taylor: Copy drafts: Tile A (claim): 'Median chat latency 90ms — feels instant.' Subline: 'Measured across 100 concurrent sessions; 95th=320ms; batching enabled.' Tile B: 'Up to 30% lower per-token spend vs baseline.' Subline: 'Typical chat workload with continuous batching and prefix cache.'
Ava: Good. We should pick a baseline (public model or prior infra). Noah, suggest a baseline and phrasing: 'vs standard open-model runtime' is too vague.
Noah: Use 'vs baseline: open-serve-1.0 on p4' in the notes, but on public facing copy just state '% reduction vs typical self-hosted setup'. Put exact numbers in appendix.
Priya: Lead routing: registrant attends + views billing slide => tag as 'engaged: webinar' and send to SDR. If they request pricing or check 'send sample prompts' checkbox => escalate to AE. HubSpot fields: email, company, company_size, token_estimate, attended(boolean), asked_question(boolean).
OpsBot: Webinar event created: 2026-06-02T18:00:00Z — Host: Ava — Draft landing slug: /benchmarks/fastpath-dollarframe
Ava: Recording plan: pre-record demo (7-8 mins) + live walkthrough (10 mins) + 25 min Q&A. Keep total under 45.
Taylor: I'll make three PNGs (desktop + mobile crops) and a small GIF showing the calculator in action. ETA: tomorrow 11:00 PT.
Leo: Deliverables: CSV + assumptions.txt + run seed. ETA: EOD PST today.
Ava: Final asks: Leo upload artifacts to the ticket, Taylor drop visuals in the drive, Priya wire UTM + HubSpot mapping, Noah draft appendix with baseline description. We'll reconvene tomorrow 09:30 PT for deck review.
Priya: I'll also draft two short email subject lines for the invite: 'See how latency saves dollars' and 'How to cut inference spend by 30% (benchmarks)'. Which is better?
Noah: Both. Test them. Second is more click-y but riskier for compliance.
Ava: Locking plan. Thanks team :rocket:
